parsed.attack: The author's own pain statement concedes the verdict: families 'churn out of the tools built for it even when the need is real.' The binding constraint on every dead caregiving-log product was the friction of logging, and this unlock addresses inference cost, which was never what people were refusing to pay. The required behaviour - two or more adult siblings each dictating thirty seconds after every call, visit and contractor, sustained for years - is the single most reliably non-occurring behaviour in consumer software, and the query it enables ('what did the furnace guy say in March') fires perhaps twice a year, far below the frequency needed to sustain any habit, let alone $8 a month. The sibling dynamic makes it worse rather than better: in the overwhelming majority of these households one sibling does most of the work and the others' non-participation is a conflict-avoidance choice, not an information gap, so a shared ledger that makes the imbalance auditable is a thing the absent sibling has an active reason to decline - which is precisely the 40% invite-acceptance metric the author has already flagged as a kill.
parsed.strongest_defence: Do not ask for dictation at all - ingest passively from the family group chat, forwarded emails and calendar entries the siblings already produce, and let the model assemble the record; the paying user is the primary carer alone, who needs the log to defend decisions to the others, so the second sibling is a bonus rather than a dependency.
parsed.verdict_reason: The product's answer to a pain made of unpaid labour is more unpaid labour, and every defence that works requires abandoning the dictation wedge as written.
